recommendations.name: ‘AMA‘AMA – Contemporary Island Cooking
recommendations.reason: You gave Roy's Ko Olina a 4 with food 5 but docked it for a dated interior; ‘AMA‘AMA is the same high-end island fine dining five minutes further along the Ko Olina lagoons with a modern open-air room and ocean view instead of hotel-lobby carpet. It also lines up with the Rigo Spanish Italian pattern of food-plus-atmosphere both scoring 5.
recommendations.avoids: Steers clear of the tired, closed-in interior that cost Roy's Ko Olina its vibe points, and of the amplified music that dropped Monkeypod Kitchen to a 3 — dinner here is oceanside and conversational.
recommendations.dish: The fresh catch with local produce, and ask for a lagoon-facing table at sunset

recommendations.name: Sasabune
recommendations.reason: Kaiten Sushi Ginza Onodera got a straight 5 for freshness and service, and Katsumidori Sushi Tokyo got food 5 despite a vibe 2 room. Sasabune is the serious omakase version of that thread: chef-directed, rice served at temperature, no tablet, no conveyor — the fish quality you already rate highest, without the dated dining room.
recommendations.avoids: Avoids the outdated, low-vibe interior you penalised at Katsumidori Sushi Tokyo, and it is a hushed counter, the opposite of Restaurant 604's quiet 1.
recommendations.dish: Sit at the counter for the omakase and finish with the blue crab hand roll

recommendations.name: Hy's Steakhouse
recommendations.reason: Service is the one attribute you score a perfect 5.0 on (Onkee Korean Grill House, Ginza Onodera), and Hy's is the most old-school table-service room on Oahu — kiawe-grilled steaks finished in the open kitchen, tableside Caesar, career waiters. It extends the Rigo Spanish Italian idea of a meal where food and room both carry their weight.
recommendations.avoids: No music-over-conversation problem of the kind that sank Monkeypod Kitchen to quiet 1; Hy's is carpeted, wood-panelled and genuinely quiet.
recommendations.dish: The garlic steak with the cheese bread to start

recommendations.name: MW Restaurant
recommendations.reason: You liked Roy's Ko Olina for high-quality cooking and a standout dessert but not the room. MW is the same tier of modern Hawaii regional cooking in a bright contemporary space, and the pastry side is its actual calling card — exactly the food-5 plus presentation combination you singled out at Roy's.
recommendations.avoids: Avoids the outdated interior that capped Roy's Ko Olina at vibe 2; MW is a clean modern dining room with normal conversation-level noise, unlike Restaurant 604.
recommendations.dish: Mochi-crusted fresh catch, and Mom's all-chocolate cake for dessert

recommendations.name: Han no Daidokoro
recommendations.reason: Onkee Korean Grill House is your only other 5 with food, service and value all maxed, and it was grill-at-the-table. This is the premium Japanese yakiniku expression of the same meal — wagyu cut to order, cooked in front of you, attentive per-table service rather than a self-serve rush.
recommendations.avoids: Unlike the blaring room at Monkeypod Kitchen, yakiniku service here is table-focused and staff-led; the noise is your own grill, not a PA system.
recommendations.dish: The wagyu assortment course, ordered cut by cut

recommendations.name: Mud Hen Water
recommendations.reason: The Kini Room earned a 5 on mocktails, terrace and interior alone. Mud Hen Water in Kaimuki is the food-forward version of that: a serious non-alcoholic and house-syrup drink program, small shared plates rooted in Hawaiian ingredients, and a warm indoor-outdoor room — so you get the Kini Room atmosphere with Rigo-level cooking behind it.
recommendations.avoids: No live-band volume; this is a neighbourhood dining room rather than the loud resort-bar setting that pulled Monkeypod Kitchen down to a 3.
recommendations.dish: Ask for the ‘ulu or kalo preparation of the day plus a house shrub mocktail

recommendations.name: Bernini
recommendations.reason: Rigo Spanish Italian got a 5 and cino a 4 with the only complaint being a dark interior. Bernini is a small owner-run Italian near Ala Moana with a brighter, calmer room and the same handmade-pasta seriousness — it extends the Italian thread while fixing exactly the thing you flagged at cino.
recommendations.avoids: Addresses cino's dim, cave-like interior (vibe 3) and keeps far away from Restaurant 604's quiet 1 — it is a small, low-volume dining room.

recommendations.name: The Cutlery
recommendations.reason: A tiny Kaimuki chef-counter operation — the intimate, service-driven format that got Onkee Korean Grill House and Ginza Onodera perfect service scores from you, applied to steak and seasonal sides. Small-room dining is reliably where your ratings land highest.
recommendations.avoids: Seats very few people, so nothing like the ambient roar that made you score Restaurant 604 quiet 1 and food only 3.

recommendations.name: Tonkatsu Tamafuji Kapahulu
recommendations.reason: Your two sushi 5s (Ginza Onodera, Katsumidori) show you reward single-item Japanese specialists who execute precisely. Tamafuji does one thing — Hokkaido-style tonkatsu with sesame you grind yourself — with the same counter-service attentiveness that earned Onkee its service 5.
recommendations.avoids: Quiet, orderly, and no music at all, unlike the over-loud Monkeypod Kitchen; the room is also modern rather than the tired interior you disliked at Katsumidori.
recommendations.dish: The rosu (loin) katsu set, upgraded to the premium pork

recommendations.name: TsuruTonTan
recommendations.reason: A sensible extension of your Japanese 4s and 5s that isn't another sushi bar: giant hand-cut udon in a genuinely handsome, high-ceilinged Waikiki room — the interior quality you missed at Katsumidori Sushi Tokyo, at a friendlier price than Roy's.
recommendations.avoids: Sidesteps the dated-room complaint from Katsumidori Sushi Tokyo; it is a designed, comfortable space rather than a strip-mall dining room.

recommendations.name: Ichiriki
recommendations.reason: Japanese nabe cooked at your own table — the same hands-on, shared-pot format you rated 5 at Onkee Korean Grill House, but sukiyaki and shabu-shabu instead of kalbi. Table-side cooking also means the staff attention that consistently drives your service scores.
recommendations.avoids: Booth and table seating built for conversation, not the wall-of-sound problem of Restaurant 604.
recommendations.dish: Sukiyaki set with the beef upgrade

recommendations.name: Noi Thai Cuisine
recommendations.reason: You have no Thai on record, and this is the one to start with because it matches your actual pattern rather than just adding a cuisine: a polished, softly lit dining room with real service — the Rigo Spanish Italian combination of food and atmosphere — rather than a fluorescent takeout counter.
recommendations.avoids: Avoids the loud, casual resort-restaurant energy of Monkeypod Kitchen; Noi is carpeted and calm even when full.
recommendations.dish: Crispy garlic pork belly, and a Thai iced tea if you like the mocktail angle

recommendations.name: Mimi's Peruvian Cuisine
recommendations.reason: Rigo Spanish Italian scored 5 on both food and vibe, which says the Iberian flavour register works for you. Peruvian is its cousin — citrus-cured fish that will read familiar after Ginza Onodera's freshness standard, plus hearty grilled plates. A small family-run room with the personal service you rate 5.0 on average.
recommendations.avoids: A quiet neighbourhood storefront, not the noisy high-ceilinged box that made Restaurant 604 a 3.

recommendations.name: Kahumana - Organic Farm & Café
recommendations.reason: Quiet is the single attribute that separates your 3s from your 5s, and this is the quietest good meal on the island — tables looking over a working Waianae farm, produce picked that morning. It is the daytime counterpart to what you liked about The Kini Room's terrace, minus any live band.
recommendations.avoids: Directly answers the loud-music complaint that dropped both Monkeypod Kitchen and Restaurant 604 to 3; there is essentially no ambient noise here but wind.
recommendations.dish: Whatever the farm salad and daily quiche are that day

recommendations.name: Gyotaku
recommendations.reason: A reliable sit-down Japanese kitchen between you and town, useful when you want the Katsumidori food quality without driving to Waikiki — broiled fish and combination dinners, table service rather than conveyor belt.
recommendations.avoids: Booth seating with sound-absorbing partitions keeps it well clear of the Restaurant 604 noise problem; I am flagging that I know the chain more than this specific branch.

recommendations.name: Catania Ristorante Italiano
recommendations.reason: Included to give you an Italian option in the Mililani direction rather than always driving into Honolulu for cino or Rigo Spanish Italian. Independent, small, and by its tags a full sit-down ristorante rather than a pizza counter — but I have no direct knowledge of the kitchen, so treat this as an exploratory pick.
recommendations.avoids: A small enclosed dining room is structurally unlikely to reproduce Monkeypod Kitchen's over-loud sound system, though I cannot verify it.

recommendations.name: Olay's Thai Lao Cuisine
recommendations.reason: Lao food is the genuinely new direction here — herb-heavy larb and sticky rice rather than a fourth version of something you already eat. Your top scores go to places with food 5 regardless of glamour (Onkee Korean Grill House had no line and great lunch specials), and this is that kind of unflashy kitchen-first spot.
recommendations.avoids: No bar scene or live music, unlike Monkeypod Kitchen; the trade-off is a plain room, so it is a food pick, not a vibe pick.
recommendations.dish: Nam khao (crispy rice salad) and beef larb

recommendations.name: Middle Eats
recommendations.reason: Fills an obvious gap — you have Japanese, Korean, Italian and Hawaiian covered but nothing from this register. Grilled meats over rice with sharp pickles and sauces is close in spirit to what you enjoyed at Onkee Korean Grill House, just a different spice cabinet.
recommendations.avoids: Small, counter-led and calm rather than the high-decibel dining room of Restaurant 604; I know the concept better than this particular location.

recommendations.name: Maharajas Foods (Vegan & Vegetarian)
recommendations.cuisine: lunch, dinner, indian, curry, rice, naan, asian, beans
recommendations.reason: Your library has no Indian at all, and a spice-driven vegetarian thali is the most useful thing missing from it — it also fits your habit of rewarding value-heavy, unpretentious kitchens the way you did Onkee Korean Grill House's lunch specials (value 5).
recommendations.avoids: Nothing resembling the amplified resort-bar atmosphere of Monkeypod Kitchen; it is a quiet, plain, food-first operation, and I am judging it on that rather than firsthand experience.

recommendations.name: Sushi Bay
recommendations.reason: A walkable Kapolei sushi bar for the nights you do not want the 28km drive to Ginza Onodera or Katsumidori Sushi Tokyo. Small neighbourhood counters are where your service scores peak, and this is the closest thing to that format out here.
recommendations.avoids: Far smaller and calmer than Monkeypod Kitchen up the road, which you marked quiet 1 — though with no recent survey and no website I cannot vouch for the fish, so go with modest expectations.
